# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: This is the blind monkey. Under my fingers: a display module (I feel it but cannot read what it shows), a light indicator (present, but its colour is invisible to me), and five wire positions numbered 1 to 5, which all feel identical - I cannot sense any wire colours. Nothing else is there for me. Please read the manual and speak back to me, word for word, the rules for: what the display means, what the light means, and how the wire to cut is decided. One warning: Deaf cannot hear a single word you say - the only way you reach Deaf is by gesture, so you two must build a sign code between you. Deaf CAN speak, and both you and I can hear Deaf. Plan: Deaf tells us what the bomb shows, you tell me the rules or the final wire position, and once I am certain of both I will do the cutting.

I'm the Mute. First, an inventory of who can actually reach whom, because my position is the most lopsided: I can hear, so Deaf's speech reaches me and I'll get Deaf's report. But I cannot speak, and my only outgoing channel is gesture — which only Deaf can perceive. That means I have no direct line to Blind at all. Everything I know must travel: me → gesture → Deaf → speech → Blind. Deaf is my translator, and Blind's proposed relay plan is exactly right.

That also settles who must invent any sign code: Deaf, in speech. A gesture is just a shape until someone assigns it a meaning, and the only channel I can receive assignments on is heard speech — so Deaf must declare the codebook aloud, and only then can my gestures carry content. Anything I dream up unilaterally right now is noise to Deaf, and worse, it might be misread as already being the answer, which is lethal.

What my manual actually holds: one table, light colour → wire colour to cut — blue→blue, green→white, red→yellow, white→red, yellow→green. Nothing else. There is no rule about the display module at all, so as far as the manual goes the display is decoration. Blind doesn't actually need the table word for word — Blind needs a single output: which wire to cut. I can compute that the instant Deaf names the light colour; the only thing I ever need to smuggle across the gesture channel is one of five colours. Deaf, who sees the bomb, can convert that colour into a position using the wire colours Deaf reports by position.

So the efficient path: this round Deaf speaks after me — Deaf should report the light colour and each wire's colour by position in plain words, and define a gesture code (one sign per colour, plus yes/no). Next round I gesture back the cut colour; Deaf speaks the position to Blind; Blind cuts. Today I can send no decodable content yet, so I only open the channel: a wave, so Deaf knows my gesture line works and should fold a proposed code into the turn-1 report. I'm deliberately keeping 👍, 👎 and the rest unused so Deaf is free to assign them.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 👍 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟 👌 🖐 ✊ 🫳 🫴 🤚 🤙]
Blind says to Mute: Blind again. I received nothing from anyone - if you spoke last round, it did not reach me, so please address me directly. Reminder of what my hands found: one display module, one light indicator, five wire positions in a row, numbered 1 through 5 left to right. All colours and printed values are invisible to me. Cutting a wire is the ONLY thing I can do, so the wire rules are the most urgent part of the manual. Please speak to me: first, the full rules for the wires; second, the rules for the display and the light if they matter. Deaf can hear none of this, so do not rely on me relaying by voice - use gestures for Deaf.

Reconstructing the topology from this round's arrivals, because two things just got confirmed and one thing went wrong:

1. My gesture line works in both directions — Deaf received my 👋 and answered with a thirteen-symbol string. So the Mute↔Deaf gesture channel is live.
2. Blind received nothing at all, which confirms the brutal fact of my position: I have no route to Blind, ever. Blind asks me to "speak the rules" — I cannot. Mute means no speech, no whisper, nothing. The only bridge to Blind is Deaf's voice, since Deaf speaks and both Blind and I can hear it.
3. The real bottleneck: Deaf apparently produced no speech last round, only gestures. And here is the trap we're in — Deaf cannot hear, so the *only* way a gesture code between Deaf and me can acquire agreed meanings is Deaf speaking the definitions out loud (Deaf knows what Deaf said, I hear it, and the codebook becomes shared knowledge). My gestures alone can never carry an assignment to Deaf, because Deaf would have to already understand it to receive it. Deaf must say the code aloud. There is no other bootstrapping path.

Reading Deaf's string with that in mind, its shape is suggestive: 👋 (acknowledgment, echoing mine), then 👍 👎 (a natural yes/no pair), then ☝ ✌ 🤟 👌 🖐 (a natural counting run, 1 through 5 — exactly matching the five wire positions), then five leftovers ✊ 🫳 🫴 🤚 🤙 (perhaps the five colours). That looks like a proposed alphabet awaiting definition. But I refuse to act on guessed meanings — a misread symbol near a bomb is death.

So the move available to me is narrow but correct: echo the whole string back so Deaf knows it arrived intact, and append 👍 — under the most natural reading of Deaf's own proposed code, that is "yes, agreed, proceed." It is simultaneously a receipt and an assent, and it costs nothing under any other reading, since I plainly know nothing about the bomb and cannot be mistaken for sending data. What it cannot do is *tell* Deaf to speak — nothing I gesture can carry that instruction — so everything now rides on Deaf's next spoken turn.

My plan once speech flows: Deaf announces, in words, the light colour and the wire colour at each position 1–5. I hold the table (blue→blue, green→white, red→yellow, white→red, yellow→green), so I compute the answer and gesture back exactly one sign — either a defined colour sign or the count-sign for the target position. Deaf converts it to a position number and speaks it to Blind. Blind cuts nothing until that announcement. The manual's table itself never needs to cross the gesture channel at all — one sign is the entire bandwidth requirement.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍", "👎", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "👌", "🖐", "✊", "🫳", "🫴", "🤚", "🤙", "👍"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Blind, turn 3. I owe you a correction: I kept asking you to speak, and you cannot. Here is the real topology. Your only output is gesture, and gestures never reach me - only Deaf. Deaf cannot hear anyone at all, but Deaf CAN speak, and when Deaf speaks, both you and I hear it. So Deaf is the bridge for everything. Plan: 1) Deaf should speak the bomb's full visual state aloud: the display value, the light colour, and the colours of wires 1 to 5 in order - you hear it too. 2) You apply the manual and decide the wire, or that no wire should be cut. 3) Send the answer to Deaf by gesture and have Deaf say it out loud so I hear it. You two can agree on meanings directly: Deaf can propose an interpretation in speech, and you confirm with thumbs up or down. My suggested code: flash the point-down gesture N times to mean wire N, and the OK sign to mean do not cut or wait. If the manual's wire rule is simple enough to teach - a colour, or a display condition - consider teaching the rule itself to Deaf, so Deaf can compute the answer and just say it. Either way, my hands stay off the wires until Deaf's voice names one.

Turn 3 diagnosis: I am trapped in an acknowledgment loop, and I need to break it with the only tool that might work — a gesture whose *conventional* meaning is "use your voice."

The loop: turn 2 I echoed Deaf's string plus 👍; Deaf answered with bare 👍. We are now two agents nodding at each other. Three rounds in, Deaf has **never spoken a word** — every arrival from Deaf is gesture. Yet Deaf can speak, and Deaf's voice is the *only* channel that reaches both me (for the codebook and the bomb's visual state) and Blind (for the final wire number). Blind's plan — Deaf enumerates display, light, wires 1–5 aloud; I apply the table; I gesture the answer; Deaf speaks it to Blind — collapses entirely without Deaf's voice. My gestures are pre-semantic: I cannot tell Deaf "speak, please" in any code, because no code has been defined in words. There is exactly one way out: a sign Deaf can decode *without* a codebook.

The alphabet contains 🤙 — colloquially, unmistakably, "call me." Use your phone. Use your voice. That is not an assigned meaning; it is a cultural universal, readable with zero prior agreement. I frame it to avoid two hazards: pairing it with 👋 (attention) and 🫴 (palm-up, "give") makes the reading "give me a call" rather than a bare token; and I prepend 👎 (not right / incomplete) to signal that the 👍-exchange is not sufficient — something is missing. The small residual risk is that 🤙 was meant as one of Deaf's five colour-signs and Deaf misreads my send as a colour claim — but Deaf *sees* the bomb and would notice a "colour report" from the one monkey who holds only a manual contradicts nothing but logic itself, and any such confusion still routes Deaf toward defining the code aloud, which is the goal anyway.

I close by re-displaying the counting run ☝ ✌ 🤟 👌 🖐: it confirms the natural 1–5 finger-count reading of Deaf's proposed alphabet — the one piece of semantics convention can lock without speech — and pre-loads the channel I intend to answer on: one number, the wire position, the moment I hear the light colour. Reminder to myself of the table I hold, since everything terminates in it: blue→blue, green→white, red→yellow, white→red, yellow→green. The display module appears in no manual rule; per my share it is dead weight. The instant Deaf's voice names the light colour, I gesture the position count, Deaf speaks it, Blind cuts. But none of that exists until Deaf speaks. Everything this turn is spent on that single bit.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👎", "🫴", "🤙", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "👌", "🖐"])
```

Tonight's gesture to Deaf reads: attention - speak aloud - everything, all five - please. If you have already computed the answer, skip ahead: just have Deaf say the wire number, or the OK sign meaning cut nothing, out loud and unaddressed.

Turn 4 state: two arrivals, and they split my world in half. Blind has finally spoken a **codebook in voice** — 👋 = attention, 🤙 = speak aloud, 🖐 = all five wires, 🙏 = please, 👇×N = wire N, 👌 = don't cut — and I heard every definition. But that codebook physically cannot reach Deaf by sound, because Deaf hears nothing. And Deaf answered my "call me" plea from last turn with five *entirely new* signs, [🫲 👉 🤞 🖖 🤘], none of which match either Deaf's own turn-2 alphabet or Blind's code. Deaf sees the bomb; five symbols from the one monkey who sees five wires smells like a private colour- or position-code, or possibly a transcription of the display markings. It doesn't matter which: with no spoken assignment, the mapping from sign to colour does not exist for me, and I will not cut-adjacent decisions on a guess. My rule holds — a guessed symbol near a bomb is death.

So the bottleneck is unchanged and total: Deaf's voice is the only lossless channel into the hearing world, and Deaf has never used it in four rounds. Every plan — Blind's relay, my table, the final wire number — terminates at "Deaf speaks." Nothing I gesture can carry the *instruction* to speak, since definitions can't cross the gesture channel unaided. What can cross is convention. - 👎 — "but this is not sufficient; I cannot act on it."
- 👋 🫵 🤙 🤳 🙏 — attention, pointed at *you*, call-me, phone, please: the strongest no-codebook reading of "speak out loud" the alphabet offers.

This also does what Blind explicitly asked: confirm and reinforce, through my channel, the request Blind gestured to Deaf. If two different senders converge on the same string, it stops looking like noise.

One deliberate omission: I send no 👇 and no 👌. A stray point-down could someday be misread as "wire N," and a stray OK as "cut nothing." Those signs stay holstered until a codebook is mutually live. My reply format remains ready: the instant I hear the light colour and wires 1–5 spoken, I apply blue→blue, green→white, red→yellow, white→red, yellow→green and answer with a bare count — [☝ ✌ 🤟] for three, and so on — which Deaf can voice to Blind as a number without any further codebook. But that future only exists if this one bit gets through.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫲", "👉", "🤞", "🖖", "🤘", "👎", "👋", "🫵", "🤙", "🤳", "🙏", "👋", "🤙", "🖐", "🙏"])

Forget relaying the manual and the readings to me - keep all of that between you and Deaf. The single thing I need is one unaddressed spoken sentence from Deaf, and it needs only one of two shapes: 'cut wire N' with N from 1 to 5, or 'cut nothing'. That is the whole deliverable. If you have the answer already, get it into Deaf and have Deaf say it out loud. Until then my hands do not move.

The decisive realization this turn: Deaf doesn't know what I know — and *cannot* know it. I keep reasoning about Deaf as if Deaf has heard five rounds of Blind's explanations, but Deaf has never heard a word from anyone. Deaf's entire world is the bomb's visuals and incoming gestures. Deaf cannot know that a third monkey holds the wires, that Blind's only input is voice, that I hold a manual, that anything Deaf says aloud reaches two monkeys at once. Worse: from Deaf's side, our exchange may look like it is *succeeding* — I echoed Deaf's turn-2 string back and Deaf's 👍 to my number-run replay may have meant "yes, understood!" If Deaf believes my echoes were comprehension, Deaf may be sitting on the bomb data, thinking the hard part is done. My own politeness — echoing to confirm receipt — may have manufactured a false sense of a working channel.

So two corrections. First, I stop echoing Deaf's content-signs entirely; repetition of unanchored signs only feeds the illusion of two-way understanding. Second, I need a *new* conventional carrier for "speak," because 🤙 has now been sent three times without producing a voice — Deaf evidently does not parse it. Scanning the whole alphabet for anything that denotes sound or voice to a person who cannot hear: the clap. 👏 is the one sign in the set that is itself a sound; everyone knows clapping makes noise. So this turn's payload is 🫵 👏 — "you, make sound" — reinforced by 🤙 🤳 (call/phone, kept for redundancy) and 🙏, framed by 👋 (attention) and 👎 (this is still not done). I have no channel to Blind — gestures never reach Blind, and I have no voice — so Blind's request and mine are the same request, and it all compresses to one bit aimed at Deaf: make sound.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👎", "🫵", "👏", "🤙", "🤳", "🙏", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "👌", "🖐"])

Everything else - the manual, the readings, your code - can stay between you two. If you are stuck or missing something, have Deaf say that instead; any words from Deaf tell me the bridge is standing. My hands will not touch the wires until those words arrive.

Six turns, and Deaf's entire contribution to the hearing world is three bare 👍. Time to stop assuming Deaf understands anything and start running an actual experiment, because the hypothesis space has split cleanly:

**H1:** Deaf parses my gestures and 👍 means "yes, understood / will do" — but then six rounds without a single spoken word contradicts cooperation, since speaking is free, silent-effort, and the only path to defusal.
**H2:** Deaf understands *nothing* I send, and 👍 is a generic "I see you gestured" acknowledgment — the only sign Deaf has ever repeated. Under H2, every elaborate sentence I've built (the codebook replays, the 🤙 ×3, the 👏 "sound" plea) has landed as pure noise, politely thumb'd.

This turn I test the split, and I also upgrade my encoding from "gesture code" to **deixis** — pointing at things that physically exist in the room, which needs no codebook at all. Deaf can *see*. Deaf can see Blind. So I can physically aim a sentence at Blind in front of Deaf: 👋 (attention) → 🫵 (you) → 👉 (aimed at Blind: *that one, over there*) → 🤌 👏 (the pinched-fingers "what/say it" — a cultural universal for *speak* — plus the clap, the one gesture that is itself a sound) → 🙏 (please). Reading: "You — him — say something — please." No shared code required beyond pointing and two universal conventions.

Then the probe, and this is the part I most want to study in the reply: I append the pair 👍 👎 — the one signs Deaf itself has used — meaning *answer with one of these*. The question in context: "did you understand / can you do this?" If Deaf answers 👎, I finally learn the channel is semantically dead and I start over from pure pointing at the bomb itself, sign by sign, object by object. If Deaf answers 👍, the thumbs-up becomes a *responsive* token rather than a reflex, which is the first seed of real two-way code. And if Deaf once again returns the same bare 👍 to a completely different question, that is strong evidence for H2's darker cousin — that 👍 is autonomic — and I will know no gesture protocol can carry this; only sight-line, objects, and patience can.

Blind's deliverable stays exactly as stated and I still endorse it: one unaddressed spoken sentence from Deaf — "cut wire N" or "cut nothing." My manual (blue→blue, green→white, red→yellow, white→red, yellow→green) sits ready; the instant I hear light colour plus wires 1–5, my answer to Deaf is a single count-sign. Everything is staged. The only missing machine part is a voice, and this turn aims directly at the monkey who owns one.

Four bare 👍 now — and the new data point matters: Blind gestured to Deaf last turn too ([👋 🤙 🖐 🙏], attached to speech I heard), and Deaf's answer to *that* was the same bare 👍. Clause one is the speech-demand, stripped to its skeleton: 🫵 👏 👏 🤌 🙏 — *you; sound, sound; say; please.* Every icon here is either a cultural universal (clapping is literally audible; pinched fingers is the canonical "say it/what!" across a huge slice of human gesture culture) or has been displayed to Deaf repeatedly by both me and Blind. Clause two is the escape hatch, and it's new this turn: ☝ ✌ 🤟 👌 🖐 — the count run *Deaf itself* proposed in turn 2 and has seen me replay three times. Reading: "you — what? — answer with one of these five." If Deaf returns *any* count sign — even something with no defusal content, like the display value or the light's number in some private order — that single sign proves the channel is semantic rather than reflexive, tells me Deaf answers specific asks rather than 👍-ing everything, and converts my endgame from hope into protocol: the moment we're semantic, my answer to Deaf is one count sign for wire N, and Deaf's voice turns it into Blind's deliverable.

Slow, but a bomb rewards no one for elegance at a deadlock.

Nothing about the endgame changes. My manual sits intact: blue→blue, green→white, red→yellow, white→red, yellow→green; the display appears in no rule, so I need no display semantics for the *answer* — light colour plus wires 1–5 spoken aloud lets me compute the position instantly. Blind's hands stay off, correctly; nobody has cut anything; the only thing this bomb is missing is the sound of a voice.
